q: for within her fane Outraged Cassandra was of Oileus son Lust-maddened.

s: Cassandra is victim of Cassandra's violation (in Athena's temple)
q: Outraged Cassandra was of Oileus son Lust-maddened.

s: Priam is a king of Troy (god-descended)
q: The burg of god-descended Priam destroyed.

s: Aeneas has a palace (in Troy)
q: Here burned Aeneas' palace

s: Aethra is a mother of Theseus (also grandmother of Demophoon and Acamas)
q: For great Zeus' sake, for your dear parents' sake, I pray you, if the seed of Theseus came Hither with Atreus' sons, O bring ye me

s: Helen is wife of Menelaus (marital relationship)
q: Forbear wrath, Menelaus, now: 'twere shame To slay thy wedded wife, for whose sake we Have suffered much affliction, while we sought Vengeance on Priam.

s: Aethra is child of Pittheus (her father)
q: In Troezen's halls Pittheus begat me

s: Aethra is wife of Aegeus (marital relationship)
q: Aegeus wedded me

s: Demophoon is son of Theseus
q: We whom thou seest are the sons of him, Thy noble son

s: Acamas is son of Theseus
q: We whom thou seest are the sons of him, Thy noble son

s: Demophoon is grandson of Aethra
q: Then his great father's mother clasped him round

s: Acamas is grandson of Aethra
q: Then his great father's mother clasped him round

s: Theseus is son of Aethra
q: And of my womb sprang Theseus glory-crowned.

s: Aethra is from Troezen (formerly a queen there)
q: In Troezen's halls Pittheus begat me

s: Aethra is brought to Hellas (to return her to her former homeland)
q: with joy to Hellas' soil Thee will we bring, where once thou wast a queen.

s: Helen is child of Zeus (divine parentage)
q: Spouse of the child of Zeus the thunder-voiced!

s: Laodice is child of Priam (daughter)
q: Then, too, affliction-burdened Priam's child, Laodice

s: Fate oversees works of men (raising the obscure and lowering the exalted)
q: For strong Fate oversees all works of men, And the renownless and obscure to fame She raises, and brings low the exalted ones.

s: Fate is unavoidable by mortals (no one can escape its nets)
q: Round these were staked The nets of Fate, which no man can escape.

s: Zeus is subject to Fate (even divine power bows to Fate)
q: Because to Fate the might of Zeus must bow

s: war and destruction is carried out through battle
q: Still on Troy's folk the Argives wreaked their wrath, And battle's issues Strife Incarnate held.

s: Deiphobus has heart full of thoughts of vengeance (against the Trojans)
q: Against the Trojans was his bold heart full Of thoughts of vengeance, which were now fulfilled

s: Deiphobus is spouse of Helen (according to Menelaus's taunt)
q: Black death hath trapped thee slain in my wife's bower!

s: Paris has died dead (before Troy's fall)
q: But he hath paid Already justice' debt, hath passed beneath Death's cold dark shadow.

s: Themis is aided by Zeus (in punishing sin)
q: Holpen of Zeus, for punishment of sin.

s: Dawn is a golden-throned heavenly being
q: Then rose from Ocean Dawn the golden-throned Up to the heavens; night into Chaos sank.

s: Menelaus leads his wife (out of the burning city)
q: Amidst of these Menelaus led his wife Forth of the burning city, having wrought A mighty triumph--joy and shame were his.

s: Menelaus is husband of Helen (reunited after Troy's fall)
q: Close-following trod she in her husband's steps

s: Helen is a all-flawless woman (renowned for exceptional beauty)
q: But the folk all around Marvelled to see the glory of loveliness Of that all-flawless woman.

s: Cassandra is a Trojan captive (assigned to Agamemnon)
q: Cassandra heavenly-fair was haled the prize Of Agamemnon

s: Agamemnon possesses Cassandra (as a captive prize of war)
q: Cassandra heavenly-fair was haled the prize Of Agamemnon

s: Neoptolemus is a son of Achilles (leader of the Argives after Troy's fall)
q: Then from their rest upsprang Achaea's sons Yearning for home. With laughter 'gan they hale Down to the sea the keels: but lo, their haste Was reined in by Achilles' mighty son

s: Neoptolemus sacrifices Polyxeina (at Achilles' tomb)
q: Into the maid's throat then he plunged the blade Of death: the dear life straightway sobbed she forth

s: Hecuba suffers sharper pain (after all her griefs)
q: Then, to crown all her griefs, yet sharper pain Fell on the heart of hapless Hecuba

s: Hecuba is transformed into a pitiful hound (from woman's form)
q: For all-unhappy Priam's queen was changed From woman's form into a pitiful hound; And all men gathered round in wondering awe. Then all her body a God transformed to stone

s: Argives is a conquerors of Troy
q: And now the Argives spoiled fair-fenced Troy, And took her boundless treasures for a prey.

s: Zeus is son of Cronos
q: Yet powerless for her help to override Fate; for not Cronos' Son can stay the hand Of Destiny

s: Zeus sanctions Fate (their deeds and judgments)
q: whose might transcendeth all The Immortals, and Zeus sanctioneth all her deeds.

s: Xanthus is immortal Immortal
q: so Xanthus' soul Was utterly whelmed in grief for Ilium made A desolation; grief undying was his, Immortal though he was.

s: Simois mourns fire (with Mount Ida and Ida's inhabitants)
q: Mourned Simois And long-ridged Ida: all who on Ida dwelt Wailed from afar the ruin of Priam's town.

s: Ida mourns fire (after Priam's city is ruined)
q: Mourned Simois And long-ridged Ida: all who on Ida dwelt Wailed from afar the ruin of Priam's town.

s: Immortals are divided over fall of Troy (some aided the Argives and others aided Troy)
q: But chafed those others which had aided Troy, Beholding Priam's city wrapped in flame

s: Sinon is honored for renown (for enduring torment from the Trojans)
q: Far-famed Sinon they extolled For that dire torment he endured of foes; Yea, song and honour-guerdons without end All rendered him

s: Horse of Tree is a ambush (used to enter Troy by guile)
q: Then the song named all heroes who passed in To ambush in the Horse of Guile, and hymned The fall of god-descended Priam's burg

s: Achilles is dead dead
q: Godlike Achilles' mighty shade, in form As when he lived, the Trojans' bane, the joy Of Greeks

s: Achilles commands Polyxeina's sacrifice (as a condition for the Argives' safe return)
q: to my tomb Be Priam's daughter Polyxeina led-- Whom as my portion of the spoil I claim-- And sacrificed thereon

s: Argives possess the spoils of Troy (taken from Troy and neighboring peoples)
q: Their wealth they laid aboard, even all the spoil Taken, or ever unto Troy they came, From conquered neighbour peoples; therewithal Whatso they took from Ilium, wherein most They joyed, for untold was the sum thereof.

s: Polyxeina is a daughter of Priam (Trojan princess and captive)
q: to my tomb Be Priam's daughter Polyxeina led

s: Antenor buries Polyxeina (near his own house by Ganymedes' shrine)
q: The old man buried her, King Priam's princess-child, nigh his own house, By Ganymedes' shrine

s: Calchas is a prophet (who foresees danger to the Argives)
q: But Calchas would not with that eager host Launch forth; yea, he had fain withheld therefrom All the Achaeans, for his prophet-soul Foreboded dread destruction looming o'er The Argives by the Rocks Capherean.

s: Calchas refuses to join the Greeks' return home (because he foresees destruction at the Capherean Rocks)
q: But Calchas would not with that eager host Launch forth

s: fall of Troy hymns The fall of god-descended Priam's burg
q: Then the song named all heroes who passed in To ambush in the Horse of Guile, and hymned The fall of god-descended Priam's burg

s: Argives seek the Greeks' return home (after the fall of Troy)
q: We have touched the goal of this long war, have won Glory, have smitten our foes and their great town! Now grant, O Zeus, to our prayers safe home-return!

s: Trojan War is long war
q: We have touched the goal of this long war

s: the Greeks' return home is delayed by Athena (through her indignation's wrath)
q: Now had the Argives all to the hallowed soil Of Hellas won, by perils of the deep Unscathed, but for Athena Daughter of Zeus The Thunderer, and her indignation's wrath.

s: storm and shipwrecks is caused by Poseidon (at Achilles' request or for his benefit)
q: Tossed the great deep, smit by Poseidon's hands For a grace to strong Achilles.

s: Capherean Rocks threaten Argives (with destruction during their return voyage)
q: Foreboded dread destruction looming o'er The Argives by the Rocks Capherean.

s: the sea is stilled by Polyxeina's sacrifice (after Achilles' demand is fulfilled)
q: Then were the waves stilled, and the blast was hushed To sleep, and all the sea-flood lulled to calm.

s: Achaean fleet carry the spoils of Troy (including captives and war trophies)
q: Their wealth they laid aboard, even all the spoil Taken, or ever unto Troy they came, From conquered neighbour peoples; therewithal Whatso they took from Ilium

s: Argives are delayed by Achilles' wrath (until Polyxeina is sacrificed)
q: But not to all the Sire vouchsafed return.

s: Troy is a city (Priam's city)
q: Then, when he saw that burg beloved destroyed, Xanthus, scarce drawing breath from bloody war, Mourned with his Nymphs for ruin fallen on Troy, Mourned for the city of Priam blotted out.

s: Troy is spoiled by Argives
q: And now the Argives spoiled fair-fenced Troy, And took her boundless treasures for a prey.

s: women of Troy are captured by Argives (as slaves after Troy's destruction)
q: Each hero led A wailing Trojan woman to his ship.

s: women of Troy are reduced to thraldom (queens, handmaids, and mothers alike)
q: So moaned Troy's daughters by their foes enslaved, Handmaid and queen made one in thraldom's lot.

s: Penthesileia is a Amazon queen
q: Came, clothed upon with beauty of Goddesses, Penthesileia--came athirst indeed For groan-resounding battle

s: Penthesileia promises to defeat Achilles (before entering battle)
q: And she such deeds she promised as no man Had hoped for, even to lay Achilles low

s: Penthesileia is killed in the Trojan War (as foretold by the Fates)
q: And ever were the ghastly-visaged Fates Thrusting her on into the battle, doomed To be her first against the Greeks--and last!

s: Achilles surpasses her own (in warrior-wasting strife)
q: Ah fool!--but little knew she him, the lord Of ashen spears, how far Achilles' might In warrior-wasting strife o'erpassed her own!

s: Hector is glory my glory (while yet he lived)
q: My glory and his noble parents' glory Was he while yet he lived

s: Hector is dead slain (killed by Achilles)
q: When godlike Hector by Peleides slain Passed, and the pyre had ravined up his flesh

s: Hector's death is a death (death in the Trojan War)
q: When godlike Hector by Peleides slain Passed, and the pyre had ravined up his flesh

s: Hector's funeral pyre consumes Hector (after his death)
q: When godlike Hector by Peleides slain Passed, and the pyre had ravined up his flesh
